gaps.sentence: He was born in ___ Netherlands, not in Belgium.
gaps.explanation: Country names that are plural or contain 'Kingdom/Republic/States' take 'the': the Netherlands.

gaps.sentence: They moved to ___ coastal town an hour south of the capital.
gaps.explanation: A coastal town — first mention of one of many.

gaps.sentence: ___ weather was so bad that the match was abandoned.
gaps.explanation: The weather is always definite in a situation.

gaps.sentence: ___ good news is that sales are up by twenty per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'News' is uncountable but takes 'the' when specified: the good news is… 'Sales' here is general, so no article.

gaps.sentence: He was elected ___ chairman of the board.
gaps.explanation: No article is used with unique roles after 'elect', 'appoint', 'become'.

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
gaps.explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ honour to meet the ambassador.
gaps.explanation: 'Honour' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an honour'.
